title: Reception First Term
overview: 1. Reception Curriculum Position Reception is the final stage of AMES Early Years, the final year of the EYFS, and the developmental bridge into Basic 1. It must not simply become Basic 1 taught one year early. AMES retains the seven interconnected EYFS areas alongside Montessori Practical Life, Sensorial Development, Christian Character Education, Outdoor Learning, Nigerian & Global Context, Continuous Provision, Inclusion & SEND and Parent Partnership. 2. Nursery to Reception Transition Nursery concluded with CONNECT -> APPLY -> CREATE -> REFLECT -> PREPARE. Reception First Term begins SETTLE -> SECURE -> DECODE -> REPRESENT -> REASON -> BECOME MORE INDEPENDENT. The guiding principle is: BUILD ON NURSERY - DO NOT RESTART CHILDREN'S LEARNING. Nursery Reception Progression Rich oral language Increasingly precise spoken language Enjoy stories Discuss, retell and comprehend Phonological awareness Systematic synthetic phonics Meaningful marks Increasingly purposeful writing Name recognition Increasing letter/sound knowledge Number sense Deeper understanding of number Small quantities Composition and comparison Explore patterns Identify, continue and create patterns Investigate Predict, observe and explain Cooperative play Sustained collaborative learning Practical Life Increasing self-management Ask questions Reason and explain Child-led exploration Child-led + carefully sequenced teaching 3. First-Term Curriculum Intent Priorities: belonging and emotional security; increasingly rich communication; structured systematic synthetic phonics; handwriting readiness, letter formation and meaningful composition; deeper quantity, number composition, comparison, pattern, shape and measure; and increasing independence in routines, resources, relationships and personal responsibilities. 4. Reception First-Term Curriculum Map Week Big Idea Main Development 1 Welcome to Reception Belonging, routines and baseline understanding 2 All About Me Identity, communication and representation 3 My Body, Health and Senses Health, movement and investigation 4 Families and Relationships Belonging, diversity and storytelling 5 Feelings, Friendship and Self-Regulation PSED and emotional literacy 6 Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Review and responsive teaching 7 My School and Community Community, roles and responsibility 8 Autumn, Weather and Change Observation and seasonal/environmental change 9 Numbers Are Everywhere Number sense and mathematical application 10 Shape, Space and Pattern Spatial reasoning and mathematical language 11 Celebrations and Traditions Culture, identity and respectful comparison 12 Christmas - The Nativity Faith, story, language and creativity 13 Look How We Have Grown Consolidation and reflection Week 1 - Welcome to Reception Develop security, belonging and confidence while establishing starting points. Build listening, conversation, help-seeking, routines, relationships, safe behaviour, turn-taking, movement, pencil/fine-motor control, daily books, rhymes, names, environmental print, sound listening, meaningful marks, quantity, counting, comparison, pattern, shape and spatial language. Practical Life includes belongings, resources and cleaning spills. Assessment principle: KNOW THE CHILD BEFORE PLANNING THE NEXT STEP. 5. Reception Phonics - First-Term Position Reception begins systematic synthetic phonics. Teaching is explicit, systematic, cumulative, well sequenced and interactive, supported by decodable reading practice. Children progressively hear phonemes, recognise corresponding graphemes, blend to read, segment spoken words for spelling, form taught graphemes and read appropriate decodable words. PHONICS MUST BE TAUGHT AS A COHERENT PROGRAMME. The exact grapheme sequence follows the school's adopted approved systematic synthetic phonics programme rather than a random 'letter of the week'. Week 2 - All About Me Develop detailed communication about identity, preferences, abilities, family, language and interests. Create an All About Me book using drawing, labels where ready, meaningful writing and dictated sentences. Explore age, quantities, height, birthdays and simple class data; discuss babyhood/growth; use detailed self-portraits and expressive movement. Character: Confidence, Gratitude and Respect. Week 3 - My Body, Health and Senses Develop accurate body, senses and health knowledge. Vocabulary may include body, skeleton, muscle, heart, senses, sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch, healthy, exercise and hygiene. Investigate senses with prediction/observation, develop gross/fine motor control, discuss hygiene, teeth, sleep, movement, food and water, reinforce body autonomy/help-seeking and use meaningful measurement/counting. Character: Responsibility and Gratitude. Week 4 - Families and Relationships Develop understanding of relationships, family diversity and personal history using inclusive language. Describe family, home, routines and memories; read/retell family stories; create cards, messages, labels and captions; explore past/present, optional family photographs and traditions; use sustained non-stereotypical home role play. Character: Love, Respect and Care. Week 5 - Feelings, Friendship and Self-Regulation Develop emotional vocabulary including frustrated, disappointed, worried, excited, calm, proud, nervous, solution and compromise. Children increasingly recognise/communicate emotions, consider perspectives, wait, negotiate, solve simple disagreements, seek support and use calming strategies. The aim is not absence of conflict but increasingly constructive response. Character: Kindness, Forgiveness and Self-Control. Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility No formal examination. Revisit routines, communication, phonics, reading, writing, number, shape, physical development, PSED and Practical Life. Determine secure phonics knowledge, blending/oral-blending needs, number understanding, fine-motor development, language needs, SEND considerations, self-regulation and independence. Intervention follows assessment rather than labels. Week 7 - My School and Community Progress towards understanding relationships and responsibilities in community. Investigate school roles, familiar occupations/services/places/transport and simple maps/routes. Root learning in Angel Montessori School, Owo, familiar roads, markets, health services, places of worship and local occupations. Use signs, labels, lists, messages, captions, routes, position, counting, sorting and practical problems. Character: Service and Responsibility. Week 8 - Autumn, Weather and Change AMES follows EYFS but does not pretend Owo experiences British seasons as Britain does. Children may learn that autumn occurs in places such as the UK while direct environmental study focuses on Nigerian weather/seasonal patterns. Compare weather, rain, sun, wind, temperature, plants, clothing and environmental change. Core idea: DIFFERENT PLACES CAN EXPERIENCE DIFFERENT WEATHER AND SEASONS. Use simple weather records, descriptions and stories. Character: Curiosity and Stewardship. Week 9 - Numbers Are Everywhere Deepen structured but practical understanding of small numbers: counting, cardinality, subitising, composition, comparison, one more/one fewer, matching and representing quantities using objects, fingers, movement, stories, images, dot patterns, frames where appropriate, numerals and practical problems. Principle: DEPTH BEFORE LARGE-NUMBER PERFORMANCE. Week 10 - Shape, Space and Pattern Investigate circles, triangles, rectangles, squares and other meaningful shapes; 3D objects through construction; position, rotation, fit, pattern, informal symmetry, length, height and capacity. Use accurate mathematical language and varied orientations/contexts. Encourage planning, building, testing and changing. Character: Persistence and Order. Week 11 - Celebrations and Traditions Explore celebrations through family, Nigerian, Christian and appropriately represented wider cultural examples without stereotyping. Vocabulary: celebration, tradition, family, special, remember, together, respect. Use stories, invitations, cards, menus, labels, pattern, counting, sharing, sequence, music, dance and design. AMES maintains Christian identity while teaching respect for differing experiences. Week 12 - Christmas: The Nativity Encounter the Nativity with greater narrative depth. Vocabulary: Nativity, Mary, Joseph, Jesus, Bethlehem, shepherd, angel, wise men, gift, journey, stable. Listen, sequence, retell, role-play, draw and write developmentally appropriate captions/messages; explore journey, position, counting, pattern, shape and sequence through songs, drama, art and construction. Character: Love, Joy, Gratitude, Giving and Hope. Week 13 - Look How We Have Grown Consolidate through books, phonics, decodable reading, writing, number, mathematical games, construction, storytelling, investigation, Practical Life and outdoor learning. Review communication, PSED, physical development, phonics, reading, writing, mathematics, Understanding the World, Expressive Arts and independence. Ask: WHAT HAS THIS CHILD LEARNED, AND WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN NEXT? 6. Reception First-Term Reading Entitlement Every child receives daily systematic phonics teaching, frequent blending practice, appropriately matched decodable reading material, daily high-quality stories, nursery rhymes/poetry/songs and rich books beyond independent decoding level. Learning to decode and learning to love/understand literature happen together. 7. Writing Progression Develop gross-motor stability, shoulder/arm strength, fine-motor control, efficient tool handling, grapheme formation, oral composition, segmenting, phonically plausible spelling attempts, labels, captions, messages, lists and story-related writing. Progression: SAY IT -> HEAR IT -> SEGMENT IT -> REPRESENT IT -> READ IT BACK. 8. Mathematics Progression Develop number through quantity, subitising, cardinality, composition, comparison, numeral recognition and one more/one fewer; numerical patterns through relationships, comparison, structure and reasoning; and retain rich shape, space, measure, position, capacity, length, height, pattern and construction experiences as essential mathematical foundations. 9. Practical Life - Reception Nursery concluded I AM BECOMING INDEPENDENT. Reception begins I CAN MANAGE MYSELF AND MY LEARNING. Children increasingly organise belongings/workspace, select and restore resources, manage hygiene, serve, pour, clean, fasten, care for the environment, follow routines, seek help and take responsibility. 10. Continuous Provision Retain high-quality Reading, Writing, Mathematics, Construction, Small World, Role Play, Creative Arts, Investigation, Practical Life, Fine Motor, Technology and Outdoor Learning provision. Adult-guided teaching becomes increasingly systematic, but play remains. MORE TEACHING DOES NOT REQUIRE LESS CHILDHOOD. 11. Outdoor Curriculum Use outdoors for gross motor, mathematics, phonics games, storytelling, writing, construction, nature, weather, investigation, gardening, collaborative challenges, measurement, creative arts and problem-solving. Outdoors remains a curriculum environment. 12. Assessment Gather understanding proportionately through interaction, observation, children's work, reading, phonics, mathematics, conversation, Practical Life and play. Identify what the child knows/can do, misconceptions, support needs and next teaching. Evidence collection must not become more important than teaching. 13. Inclusion & SEND Maintain HIGH EXPECTATION + APPROPRIATE ACCESS. Support may include visual schedules, adapted resources, language modelling, smaller groups, sensory/physical adjustments, communication support, extra phonological practice, repetition, processing time and targeted intervention. Home language is an asset; limited English does not automatically indicate limited thinking. 14. First-Term Parent Partnership Explain Reception learning beyond worksheet-heavy expectations. Home partnership emphasises shared reading, school reading practice, phonics guidance consistent with the adopted programme, conversation, rhymes, meaningful writing, counting, games, independence, sleep, attendance and punctuality. 15. First-Term Expectations Depending on starting points, children increasingly settle confidently; communicate/listen; manage routines/emotions/friendships; develop movement and fine motor; participate in systematic phonics; blend/segment; recognise taught graphemes; engage with decodable text and rich literature; form graphemes and write simply; understand small-number quantities deeply; subitise, compare and compose; recognise/extend patterns; reason about shape/space; observe/investigate/create/collaborate; and take greater responsibility. These are developmental expectations, not rigid pass/fail criteria. 16. Progression Into Second Term Reception First Term: SETTLE -> SECURE -> DECODE -> REPRESENT -> REASON. Second Term moves towards DEEPEN -> READ -> COMPOSE -> INVESTIGATE -> APPLY, strengthening phonics, decodable reading, comprehension, sentence composition, handwriting, number composition, mathematical reasoning, scientific enquiry, community/world knowledge, creative design, self-regulation and independence. Reception First-Term Declaration We will protect the integrity of the EYFS. We will teach systematically where systematic teaching matters. We will teach phonics properly, read to children every day, help them decode and understand, develop writers through language and meaning, teach mathematics for understanding, investigate, build, create, talk, listen, move and go outdoors. We will preserve continuous provision, strengthen Practical Life and responsibility, respect different starting points, identify barriers early, work with families, root children in Owo and Nigeria while widening their world, and live Christian character. RECEPTION IS SCHOOL - BUT IT IS STILL EARLY YEARS. READERS - WRITERS - MATHEMATICIANS - COMMUNICATORS - THINKERS - CREATORS - PROBLEM-SOLVERS - INDEPENDENT LEARNERS HOW DOES THIS HELP THE CHILD FLOURISH? IN GOD WE TRUST.
